blocks.text: Use const by default, let only when the variable must be reassigned, and avoid var in new code. const signals to readers that the binding never changes, which makes code easier to reason about.

blocks.code:
const taxRate = 0.2;      // never reassigned
let total = 100;          // will change
total = total * (1 + taxRate);

taxRate = 0.3;            // TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.
const name;               // SyntaxError: const must be initialized

blocks.text: Block Scope and the Temporal Dead Zone

let and const are hoisted too, but stay uninitialized until their declaration line runs. The region before that line is the temporal dead zone (TDZ); touching the variable there throws. This turns silent undefined bugs into loud errors.
const freezes the binding (which value the name points to), not the value. Objects and arrays declared with const can still be mutated.

items: Names may contain letters, digits, _ and $, but cannot start with a digit.
Case-sensitive: total and Total are different variables.
Reserved words (let, class, return, if...) cannot be names.
Convention: camelCase for variables and functions, PascalCase for classes, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for true constants such as MAX_RETRIES.

blocks.text: Assigning to an undeclared name (count = 1 without let/const) silently creates a global variable in sloppy mode. In strict mode and in ES modules it throws a ReferenceError, which is one reason modern code runs in strict mode.
